short: Intrinsically Nonflammable Ionic Liquid-Based Localized High
title: Intrinsically Nonflammable Ionic Liquid-Based Localized Highly Concentrated Electrolytes Enable High-Performance Li-Metal Batteries

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Li-metal batteries need an electrolyte that is nonflammable and suppresses Li dendrite growth. Diluting the LiFSI ionic-liquid electrolyte with nonflammable HFE should cut viscosity and raise conductivity.
states.detail: Absorbed: h1 (HYP/need), h2 (HYP/hypothesis), d1 (DES/base_system), d2 (DES/modification), d4 (DES/down_select), p1 (PRC/synthesis), p2 (PRC/deposition)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: In LHCE Li+ is coordinated by FSI- as CIPs and AGGs, with HFE and PP13+ outside the sheath. The SEI formed in ILE and LHCE is inorganic, holding LiF, Li2O and S=O compounds, not carbonates.
states.detail: Absorbed: e1 (STR/chemistry/bonding), e2 (STR/chemistry/composition), e3 (STR/microstructure/shape). Premises: A Li+-coordinated FSI- S=O band sits at higher wavenumber than the free FSI- band

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: LHCE viscosity drops to about 7 mPa s, the lowest of the IL-based series. LHCE ionic conductivity reaches about 3.2 mS cm-1, roughly three times that of the ILE.
states.detail: Absorbed: v1 (PRP/value), v2 (PRP/value), v3 (PRP/behavior_class), v4 (PRP/value), m1 (MEC/pathway), m2 (MEC/pathway), m3 (MEC/pathway). Premises: The LUMO is the orbital attacked by electrons, so the lowest-LUMO species decomposes first; Inorganic LiF- and Li2O-rich SEI layers are mechanically strong and suppress dendrite growth

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Li symmetric cell with LHCE cycles stably for 1000 h at 10 mA cm-2 and 1 mAh cm-2. LFP full cell with LHCE keeps 87% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 5 C

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: A nonflammable IL-based LHCE gives dendrite-free Li plating and long-lived, safer Li-metal batteries

nodes.title: MICRO, F3
nodes.head: Deposit is needle-like and porous in commercial, nodular in ILE, flat and dense in LHCE
nodes.solves: Li plated in LHCE is flat, smooth and dense; it is dendritic in commercial and nodular in ILE
nodes.note: the optical insets of panels a, c and e show a dull uneven disc for commercial and ILE and a uniformly bright metallic disc for LHCE; the LHCE cross-section layer is visibly the thinnest
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for e3 (o11).

nodes.title: evidence, F1
nodes.head: The FSI- S=O band moves to higher wavenumber from pure IL to ILE to LHCE. The 1.95 A Li-O_FSI RDF peak grows from g(r) about 17 in ILE to about 29 in LHCE.
nodes.solves: In LHCE Li+ is coordinated by FSI- as CIPs and AGGs, with HFE and PP13+ outside the sheath
nodes.op: compare across conditions, compare coplotted quantities
nodes.note: dashed lines on the panel mark free FSI- and Li+-coordinated FSI-; the HFE bands at 840-860 cm-1 sit at the same position in pure HFE and in LHCE; the text quotes 1216, 1223 and 1227 cm-1 the Li-N_PP13 curves carry only a broad rise of g(r) about 2.5 beyond 6 A CIP share falls from about 53% (ILE) to about 47% (LHCE)
nodes.detail: o4: The FSI- S=O band moves to higher wavenumber from pure IL to ILE to LHCE; o5: The 1.95 A Li-O_FSI RDF peak grows from g(r) about 17 in ILE to about 29 in LHCE; o6: No first-shell RDF peak appears for the Li-O_HFE or Li-N_PP13 pairs; o7: AGG share rises from about 33% to about 47% and free FSI- falls from about 14% to about 7%
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for e1 (o4, o5, o6, o7).

nodes.title: evidence, F4
nodes.head: F 1s shows only the LiF peak for ILE and LHCE while the commercial spectrum also shows POF. O 1s shows S=O and Li2O for LHCE but ROCO2Li and Li2CO3 for the commercial electrolyte.
nodes.solves: The SEI formed in ILE and LHCE is inorganic, holding LiF, Li2O and S=O compounds, not carbonates
nodes.note: the LHCE LiF peak is the tallest of the three the ILE trace carries the S=O component only the text credits both ILE and LHCE with Li2O; a weak Li2O peak is also drawn for the commercial sample
nodes.detail: o12: F 1s shows only the LiF peak for ILE and LHCE while the commercial spectrum also shows POF; o13: O 1s shows S=O and Li2O for LHCE but ROCO2Li and Li2CO3 for the commercial electrolyte; a3: A Li2O component is resolved only in the LHCE O 1s trace, not in the ILE trace
nodes.inner_audit: a3: the text credits both ILE and LHCE with Li2O; a weak Li2O peak is also drawn for the commercial sample

nodes.title: evidence, F1
nodes.head: Viscosity falls from about 150 mPa s for the ILE to about 7 mPa s at IL:HFE 1:2
nodes.solves: LHCE viscosity drops to about 7 mPa s, the lowest of the IL-based series
nodes.note: log axis; the commercial bar sits at about 6 mPa s, just below the 1:2 LHCE
nodes.detail: o1: Viscosity falls from about 150 mPa s for the ILE to about 7 mPa s at IL:HFE 1:2
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for v1 (o1).

nodes.title: evidence, F1
nodes.head: Ionic conductivity of the IL series rises from about 0.7 to about 3.4 mS cm-1 as HFE is added. The commercial electrolyte holds the highest conductivity of the panel, about 8 mS cm-1
nodes.solves: LHCE ionic conductivity reaches about 3.2 mS cm-1, roughly three times that of the ILE
nodes.note: the text compares the LHCE conductivity only with the ILE, never with the commercial electrolyte
nodes.detail: o2: Ionic conductivity of the IL series rises from about 0.7 to about 3.4 mS cm-1 as HFE is added; a1: The commercial electrolyte holds the highest conductivity of the panel, about 8 mS cm-1
nodes.inner_audit: a1: the text compares the LHCE conductivity only with the ILE, never with the commercial electrolyte

nodes.title: evidence, F1
nodes.head: The commercial electrolyte ball burns with a large flame while the LHCE ball does not ignite
nodes.solves: The LHCE is intrinsically nonflammable, unlike the commercial carbonate electrolyte
nodes.detail: o3: The commercial electrolyte ball burns with a large flame while the LHCE ball does not ignite
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for v3 (o3).

nodes.title: evidence, F2
nodes.head: Coulombic efficiency holds near 99.4% over 800 cycles in LHCE against 98.8% in ILE. The ILE efficiency trace runs near 99% out to about 600 cycles after one dip near cycle 230
nodes.solves: Li plating and stripping in LHCE runs at about 99.4% Coulombic efficiency over 800 cycles
nodes.note: 99.4% and 98.8% are printed in the inset; the commercial trace peaks near 85% and collapses by cycle 80 the text says the ILE holds only until 250 cycles; this panel shows the failure only as the single dip
nodes.detail: o8: Coulombic efficiency holds near 99.4% over 800 cycles in LHCE against 98.8% in ILE; a2: The ILE efficiency trace runs near 99% out to about 600 cycles after one dip near cycle 230
nodes.inner_audit: a2: the text says the ILE holds only until 250 cycles; this panel shows the failure only as the single dip

nodes.title: evidence, F4
nodes.head: The lowest unoccupied states above the gap belong to FSI-, marked LUMO at FSI-
nodes.solves: FSI- carries the lowest unoccupied states, so it is reduced first and builds the SEI
nodes.note: HFE states start higher and weaker; PP13+ states are nearly flat
nodes.detail: o14: The lowest unoccupied states above the gap belong to FSI-, marked LUMO at FSI-
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for m1 (o14).

nodes.title: evidence, F2
nodes.head: Voltage stays within about +/-0.15 V for 1000 h; the 500 h and 1000 h insets coincide
nodes.solves: Li symmetric cell with LHCE cycles stably for 1000 h at 10 mA cm-2 and 1 mAh cm-2
nodes.note: the first 50 h show a decaying envelope up to about +/-0.6 V
nodes.detail: o10: Voltage stays within about +/-0.15 V for 1000 h; the 500 h and 1000 h insets coincide
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for g1 (o10).

nodes.title: evidence, F5
nodes.head: Capacity retention of the LHCE cell is 87% after 1000 cycles at 5 C. Coulombic efficiency of the LHCE cell stays near 100% through the 1000 cycles at 5 C.
nodes.solves: LFP full cell with LHCE keeps 87% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 5 C
nodes.op: compare across conditions, read characteristic point
nodes.note: the value is printed on the panel; the LHCE trace runs from about 105 to about 92 mAh g-1 and the ILE falls from about 46 to about 20 the efficiency trace is plotted against the right-hand axis and is labelled CE: LHCE the two traces separate only after about 400 cycles, when the commercial cell begins to fade
nodes.detail: o16: Capacity retention of the LHCE cell is 87% after 1000 cycles at 5 C; o17: Coulombic efficiency of the LHCE cell stays near 100% through the 1000 cycles at 5 C; a4: The commercial cell matches or exceeds the LHCE capacity for the first about 400 cycles at 5 C
nodes.inner_audit: a4: the two traces separate only after about 400 cycles, when the commercial cell begins to fade

nodes.title: evidence, F5
nodes.head: LHCE discharge capacity matches the commercial cell up to 5 C and exceeds it at 10 C
nodes.note: at 10 C about 79 (LHCE), 45 (commercial) and 22 mAh g-1 (ILE); ILE is lowest at every rate
nodes.detail: o15: LHCE discharge capacity matches the commercial cell up to 5 C and exceeds it at 10 C
